summary:
The kit's core does not need a third-party animation library. Top data-journalism teams confirm this: the Pudding's svelte-starter has no animation dependency, and its Scrolly helper is about 80 lines of raw IntersectionObserver. Reuters' graphics-components uses only svelte-intersection-observer plus dotLottie. Chart motion should come from the already-vendored ECharts 6.1.0 (animationDurationUpdate, universalTransition, emphasis focus/blur). DOM motion should come from CSS transitions, WAAPI, IntersectionObserver and the View Transitions API, which became Baseline in October 2025 and was verified working under file:// in Chromium 141. The existing kit/core/rk.motion.js is the right base. It needs five additions: a beforeprint hook that mounts every lazily-mounted chart with animation off (otherwise charts outside the viewport print blank); a live listener for prefers-reduced-motion changes; an RK.motion.swap() wrapper around View Transitions; screen-reader-safe count-up; and skipping animation in hidden tabs.

GSAP 3.15.0 is free for commercial use under Webflow's 2025 Standard 'No Charge' License. That license is not OSI-approved, Webflow can amend or terminate it, and it bans use in no-code visual animation builders, so it should be avoided as a dependency. If a JS animation engine is ever needed, use MIT Motion 14.2.0: a motion/mini + inView + stagger IIFE built with esbuild is only 4.4 KB gz, versus 51 KB for the full UMD. anime.js 4.5.0 (MIT, 40.6 KB gz UMD) is the alternative for rich timelines.

For UI controls, adopt Tom Select 2.6.2 (Apache-2.0, 17.6 KB gz), noUiSlider 15.8.1 (MIT, 9.4 KB) and Floating UI 1.8.0 (MIT, 8.4 KB for core plus dom), with CSS anchor positioning (Baseline since January 2026) as a progressive enhancement. For dates, use native inputs with period presets, and Air Datepicker 3.6.0 only when a calendar is truly needed. Several candidates are now unmaintained or archived and should be avoided: flatpickr (last release 2022), Tippy (archived 2024-11), Shoelace (archived), Pico (archived 2026-10-04), AOS (last release 2018) and typed.js (now GPL-3.0). Web Awesome only ships ES modules, which fail to load under file://.

For icons, use Lucide 1.57.0 (ISC) as the primary set and Tabler Icons 3.49.0 (MIT, 366 finance/chart glyphs) as a secondary set. The Python builder must inline only the icons a report uses as a <symbol> sprite, because Chromium blocks external sprite references under file://.

For fonts: Fontsource's Inter keeps tnum (so the kit's tabular-nums CSS works) but drops zero, case and the ss/cv stylistic sets. Upstream inter-ui 4.1.1 provides a ~100 KB variable latin subset with every feature. Pair it with Source Serif 4 for headings and Noto Sans SC for Chinese. Noto Sans SC has no Reserved Font Name, so the builder can subset it to the report's text; Plex and Source fonts do reserve their names, so they should not be self-subset under the original name.

libraries.name: GSAP (+ScrollTrigger, SplitText)
libraries.capabilities: Best-in-class timeline tween engine; ScrollTrigger pin/scrub, Flip (FLIP layouts), SplitText, MorphSVG, DrawSVG — all plugins now free
libraries.interactions_animation: Timelines, scroll-linked scrub/pin, FLIP, SVG morph/draw, text split
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes: dist/gsap.min.js -> window.gsap, dist/ScrollTrigger.min.js -> ScrollTrigger (verified file:// Chromium 141)
libraries.size: 28.3 KB gz core; 45.6 KB gz with ScrollTrigger
libraries.reason: Legally OK for commercial client sites, but non-OSI license that Webflow can amend/terminate at discretion, bans use in no-code visual animation builders competing with Webflow (grey zone if kit grows configurable motion in Step 2), redistribution not expressly granted. Violates project 'permissive only' rule; use as design reference only.

libraries.name: anime.js v4
libraries.capabilities: animate, createTimeline, stagger (grid/3D/jitter), onScroll, createLayout (FLIP), splitText, scrambleText, svg drawables/morph, springs, draggable, waapi.animate, registerAdapter
libraries.interactions_animation: Full-featured MIT timeline engine; WAAPI mode for GPU-accelerated tweens
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes: dist/bundles/anime.umd.min.js -> window.anime (verified)
libraries.size: 40.6 KB gz full UMD; 17.0 KB gz esbuild IIFE subset (animate/stagger/timeline/utils); 7.8 KB gz waapi+stagger
libraries.reason: Best MIT all-in-one if story pages need rich timelines/SVG draw; v4.x minor versions had breaking changes (4.4.0) so pin exactly. Not needed for core report motion.

libraries.name: Motion (motion.dev, ex-Framer Motion) vanilla
libraries.license: MIT (Motion+ is a separate paid product)
libraries.capabilities: animate (hybrid WAAPI/JS engine, springs), animateView (View Transitions wrapper with springs/interrupt queue), inView, scroll, stagger, hover/press gestures
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes: dist/motion.js UMD -> window.Motion (verified). motion/mini subset needs esbuild IIFE prebuild
libraries.size: 51.3 KB gz full UMD; 4.4 KB gz IIFE of motion/mini animate + inView + stagger
libraries.reason: Preferred optional JS engine via a 4.4 KB motion/mini IIFE when springs/sequences are needed; fast major-version churn (v12->v14 in ~1 yr) requires exact pinning.

libraries.name: Web platform motion: WAAPI + IntersectionObserver + View Transitions API
libraries.latest_version: same-document View Transitions Baseline 2025-10 (Chrome 111, Safari 18, Firefox 144)
libraries.capabilities: element.animate()/finished/getAnimations, IO reveal & lazy chart mount, document.startViewTransition for filter/tab/re-sort transitions, @starting-style for dialog/popover entry
libraries.interactions_animation: FLIP-style re-layout on filter change, staggered reveal, print-time finish()
libraries.offline_classic_script: Native; startViewTransition verified working under file:// (Chromium 141)
libraries.reason: Zero dependency, matches how Pudding/Reuters build motion, works offline, respects reduced-motion; wrap in RK.motion.swap() with fallback for older locked-down corporate browsers.

libraries.name: CSS scroll-driven animations (animation-timeline: scroll()/view())
libraries.latest_version: Chrome 115+, Safari 26+; Firefox stable still behind flag (not Baseline)
libraries.capabilities: Declarative scroll-progress and view-progress linked animations without JS
libraries.interactions_animation: Reading progress bars, decorative parallax-free reveals
libraries.offline_classic_script: Native CSS; supported in Chromium 141 test
libraries.reason: Progressive enhancement only inside @supports with final state as default; never tie key numbers to scroll scrub.

libraries.name: Lenis (smooth scroll)
libraries.capabilities: Wheel/touch smoothing on native scroll, snap add-on
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes: dist/lenis.min.js -> globalThis.Lenis (verified)
libraries.reason: Scroll-jacking conflicts with ECharts dataZoom/Leaflet wheel zoom (needs data-lenis-prevent everywhere), hurts accessibility and feels imprecise for bankers; Locomotive v5 is built on it (same verdict).

libraries.name: Scrollama
libraries.capabilities: IntersectionObserver-based scrollytelling: step enter/exit, progress, offset, debug, built-in ResizeObserver
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes: build/scrollama.min.js -> window.scrollama (verified)
libraries.reason: Tiny, stable API (repo active 2025-11) but npm release from 2022; a ~60-80 line RK.scrolly using raw IO + position:sticky (Pudding pattern) is equally good and keeps zero deps.

libraries.name: AOS (Animate On Scroll)
libraries.capabilities: data-aos attribute scroll reveal presets
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes: dist/aos.js -> window.AOS
libraries.reason: Unreleased since 2018 (3.0 beta never shipped); RK.motion.reveal already does IO + class + stagger + reduced-motion + print override.

libraries.name: CountUp.js
libraries.capabilities: Animated number count-up with separators, decimals, Indian grouping, numerals, scroll spy/autoAnimate, plugins
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes: dist/countUp.umd.js -> countUp.CountUp (verified)
libraries.reason: Kit already has RK.motion.countUp tied to RK.format codes (must stay consistent with kit formatting); borrow ideas (scroll-spy once, smart easing).

libraries.name: NumberFlow
libraries.capabilities: <number-flow> custom element: per-digit odometer-style transitions with Intl.NumberFormat
libraries.interactions_animation: Digit roll on data change (KPI updates after filters)
libraries.offline_classic_script: No UMD (ESM/CJS only); esbuild IIFE prebuild works (5.2 KB gz)
libraries.reason: Elegant professional data-change animation for KPI tiles; requires an IIFE build step at vendor time.

libraries.name: lottie-web / dotlottie-web
libraries.capabilities: After Effects (Bodymovin) JSON animation playback (SVG/canvas)
libraries.offline_classic_script: lottie_light.min.js -> window.lottie works, but only with animationData (path: XHR blocked under file://, verified); dotlottie-web is ESM + 1.2 MB WASM, fails offline
libraries.reason: Large, low value for reports, slowing upstream; dotLottie unusable under file://. Only for brand-supplied cover animations.

libraries.name: Tom Select
libraries.capabilities: Searchable single/multi select, tags, optgroups, create, remote load, plugins (remove_button, checkbox_options, clear_button, dropdown_input, virtual_scroll)
libraries.interactions_animation: Filter dropdowns for tickers/regions/sectors; remote search for Step 2 API
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes: dist/js/tom-select.complete.min.js -> window.TomSelect (verified init under file://)
libraries.reason: Most capable vanilla select, active (2026-07), permissive license, complete build includes all plugins.

libraries.name: Choices.js
libraries.capabilities: Select/text input enhancement, multi-select, search variants (basic/kmp/prefix builds)
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes: public/assets/scripts/choices.min.js -> window.Choices (verified)
libraries.reason: Solid MIT alternative to Tom Select; slightly larger, more consumer-style default skin.

libraries.name: Slim Select
libraries.capabilities: Lightweight searchable select with multi/optgroups
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes: dist/slimselect.js UMD / slimselect.iife.js -> window.SlimSelect (verified)
libraries.reason: Very active but smaller community; no advantage over Tom Select.

libraries.name: noUiSlider
libraries.capabilities: Dual-handle range slider, steps, margin/limit, pips, tooltips, custom format, keyboard a11y
libraries.interactions_animation: Range filters (market cap, P/E, year range); sync with ECharts dataZoom
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes: dist/nouislider.min.js -> window.noUiSlider (verified init)
libraries.reason: De-facto standard range slider, tiny, mature API; no native dual-thumb alternative.

libraries.name: flatpickr
libraries.capabilities: Date/range/time picker, locales
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes: dist/flatpickr.min.js -> window.flatpickr (verified)
libraries.reason: Still works but no release since 2022 and repo inactive since 2024-08; risky for long-lived client deliverables.

libraries.name: Air Datepicker
libraries.capabilities: Date/range picker with day/month/year views, zh/en locales, CSS variables
libraries.interactions_animation: Calendar range filter when native inputs are insufficient
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes: air-datepicker.js UMD -> window.AirDatepicker (verified load); npm tarball lacks LICENSE file (fetch from GitHub)
libraries.reason: Smallest maintained calendar with range + month/year views; primary approach should be period presets + native <input type=month/date>.

libraries.name: Vanilla Calendar Pro
libraries.capabilities: Feature-rich calendar (multi-month, range, time, annotations)
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes: index.js UMD -> window.VanillaCalendarPro.Calendar (verified load)
libraries.reason: Active and capable but heavier than Air Datepicker.

libraries.name: Floating UI (dom + core)
libraries.capabilities: computePosition with offset/flip/shift/arrow/size middleware, autoUpdate
libraries.interactions_animation: Tooltips/popovers/column menus for DOM components (charts have own tooltips)
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes: floating-ui.core.umd.min.js -> FloatingUICore (load first), floating-ui.dom.umd.min.js -> FloatingUIDOM (verified)
libraries.reason: Tiny, active, the successor to Popper/Tippy; use CSS anchor positioning + popover (Baseline Jan 2026) as progressive path, Floating UI as fallback for older corporate browsers.

libraries.name: Tippy.js
libraries.capabilities: Tooltip/popover on Popper v2
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes: dist/tippy-bundle.umd.min.js + @popperjs/core umd
libraries.reason: Repository archived 2024-11-09 (read-only); use Floating UI.

libraries.capabilities: Drag-and-drop reorder lists/grids, cross-list groups, handles, built-in FLIP animation
libraries.interactions_animation: Reorder dashboard tiles, table columns, 'my metrics' lists
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes: Sortable.min.js -> window.Sortable (verified)
libraries.reason: Mature MIT; optional when user-customizable layouts are needed.

libraries.capabilities: Web-component UI library (buttons, dialogs, selects, tabs...), owned by Fonticons/Font Awesome

libraries.name: Pico.css
libraries.capabilities: Classless/semantic minimal CSS framework
libraries.offline_classic_script: CSS only (pico.min.css)

libraries.capabilities: Bootstrap-5-based admin dashboard UI kit

libraries.size: 39 KB gz JS + very large CSS

libraries.name: Lucide
libraries.capabilities: ~1890 unique 24px stroke icons (2154 files incl. aliases), 125 finance/chart-ish (chart-candlestick, banknote, trending-*)

libraries.capabilities: 5184 outline + 1054 filled icons, 366 finance/chart-ish (chart-candle, chart-bubble, building-bank, report-money, currency-*)

libraries.name: Phosphor Icons
libraries.capabilities: 1512 icons x 6 weights (thin/light/regular/bold/fill/duotone)
libraries.offline_classic_script: Icon font CSS per weight works locally, but src/index.js injects stylesheets from jsDelivr CDN (breaks offline) - must link local src/<weight>/style.css
libraries.size: ~150 KB woff2 + 78 KB css per weight

libraries.name: Heroicons / Font Awesome Free
libraries.license: MIT (Heroicons); Font Awesome Free 7.3.1 = CC-BY-4.0 AND OFL-1.1 AND MIT
libraries.capabilities: Heroicons: 324 outline icons, 36 finance-ish; FA Free: ~2000 icons
libraries.offline_classic_script: SVG files (inline as sprite)
libraries.reason: Heroicons too small a set for finance; Font Awesome Free icons require CC-BY attribution and have a dated web-2.0 look.

libraries.name: Inter (upstream inter-ui / Fontsource)
libraries.capabilities: Variable opsz+wght UI sans; upstream latin subset keeps tnum, zero, case, ss01-08, cv01-13, sups/sinf; Fontsource subset keeps only tnum/pnum/frac (fontTools-verified); default digits proportional

libraries.size: 50.9 KB wght latin; 122 KB opsz latin
libraries.reason: Pitchbook-grade serif already chosen by kit; RFN means do not self-subset under original name - use published files and ship upstream OFL text (Fontsource LICENSE only says 'Google Inc.').

libraries.name: Noto Sans SC
libraries.capabilities: Simplified Chinese variable wght; 101 unicode-range chunks so browser loads only needed glyph ranges
libraries.offline_classic_script: woff2 chunks with relative url() work offline; or builder-time pyftsubset to report text
libraries.size: 4.50 MB all chunks (static 31.75 MB); per-report subset typically <200 KB
libraries.reason: Free OFL CJK with no RFN, so Python builder can subset to exactly the report's characters; system CJK fonts as runtime fallback for API/LLM text.

libraries.name: IBM Plex Sans / Serif / Mono (/ Sans SC)
libraries.capabilities: Corporate grotesque with tabular digits by default; upstream has zero/onum/ss01-06; Sans SC matches Latin
libraries.offline_classic_script: woff2 @font-face
libraries.size: 22.6 KB/weight latin; Plex Sans SC ~3.8 MB per weight unsplit
libraries.reason: Strong alternative theme font (tabular by default); RFN 'Plex' restricts self-subsetting; Plex Sans SC too heavy.

libraries.name: JetBrains Mono
libraries.capabilities: Variable monospace for code/formula input
libraries.offline_classic_script: woff2 @font-face
libraries.reason: Only for the client formula/expression editor; tables should use proportional Inter with tnum, not monospace (Roboto Mono is an equivalent alternative).

libraries.name: CodeMirror 6
libraries.capabilities: Code editor with autocomplete, syntax highlighting, linting - candidate for client formula input
libraries.interactions_animation: Formula editing with token highlight & autocomplete
libraries.offline_classic_script: No: ESM-only; must be pre-bundled to IIFE with esbuild at vendor time
libraries.reason: Best-quality formula editor but heavy and ESM-only; cross-reference with the formula/query angle; lightweight textarea + rk.expr tokenizer may suffice.

key_insights: file:// empirical test (Playwright Chromium 141): all 20 UMD/IIFE builds load and initialize as classic scripts; <script type=module>, fetch() and XHR of local JSON are all blocked; data must ship as .js (window.RK_DATA=...).

External SVG sprite is blocked under file:// ('file: URLs are treated as unique security origins'); inline sprites, , CSS background-image and (Chromium) mask-image work -> Python builder must inline only the icons actually used.
Lottie path: loading fails under file:// (XHR); only animationData from a .js wrapper works. dotLottie (ESM + WASM) cannot run offline.

Fonts in a fonts/ subfolder load under file:// in Chromium; Firefox fixed file:// font loading in 68.0.2/70 (bug 1565942), but fonts must sit in the document's directory or a subdirectory, never a parent directory. Offer a --embed-fonts base64 option as a fallback.

Top data-journalism stacks (Pudding svelte-starter, Reuters graphics-components) ship NO animation library: framework transitions/d3 + raw IntersectionObserver + sticky layout. Pudding's Scrolly is ~80 lines of IO.

Professional motion rules: 100-500ms UI (NN/g), chart entry 400-700ms with 30-60ms stagger and <=900ms total, data updates tween from old to new values (ECharts animationDurationUpdate + universalTransition), ease-out on entry and faster exits, staged transitions for complex changes (Heer & Robertson 2007). Avoid parallax, bounce/elastic, scroll-jacking, scroll-scrubbed key numbers, typewriter effects, looping motion.

Gap in kit/core/rk.motion.js: charts that mount on scroll will print or export to PDF blank. Add beforeprint/matchMedia('print') hooks that mount all charts with animation:false, call document.getAnimations().forEach(a=>a.finish()), then resize. For Playwright PDF export use emulateMedia({media:'print', reducedMotion:'reduce'}).

Other rk.motion additions: listen to prefers-reduced-motion changes; add a ?motion=off URL flag; add an RK.motion.swap() View Transitions wrapper for all filter re-renders; make count-up screen-reader safe (aria-label holds the final value); tween counts from the old value; skip animation when document.hidden.

GSAP's 2025 Webflow license dropped the old 'cannot charge end users' clause but is still non-OSI: amendable at any time, terminable at Webflow's discretion, and it bans use in no-code visual animation builders that compete with Webflow. Many web articles still quote the obsolete clause.

ESM-only libraries can be vendored as IIFE with esbuild at vendor time (measured): motion/mini animate + inView + stagger = 4.4 KB gz; anime.js subset = 17 KB gz (vs 40.6 KB full); number-flow = 5.2 KB gz. Extend tools/vendor.py with a 'build' entry type so the runtime never needs a bundler.

Fontsource (Google Fonts-derived) woff2 subsets strip most OpenType features (verified with fontTools). Inter keeps only tnum/pnum/frac (no zero/case/ss/cv) and has proportional default digits, so the kit's tabular-nums CSS still works. Upstream inter-ui 4.1.1 variable-latin subset (~100 KB) keeps every feature. IBM Plex, Source Serif 4, Source Sans 3 and Noto Sans SC have tabular digits by default.

OFL Reserved Font Names: IBM Plex reserves 'Plex' and Adobe Source fonts reserve 'Source', so don't self-subset them under the original name. Inter, Noto Sans SC (noto-cjk), JetBrains Mono and Roboto Mono have no RFN, so the builder can subset them freely. Fontsource LICENSE files sometimes list only 'Google Inc.' as copyright holder, so ship the upstream OFL text.

Recommended CJK strategy: use the builder to pyftsubset Noto Sans SC down to the report's own text (typically <200 KB), fall back to system CJK fonts for dynamic text, and optionally include the 101-chunk unicode-range set (4.5 MB) for full coverage.

Maintenance red flags found: Pico.css archived 2026-10-04 (no longer maintained), Tippy.js archived 2024-11-09, Shoelace archived (moved to Web Awesome), flatpickr has not released since 2022, AOS since 2018, and typed.js is now GPL-3.0.

Platform status (2026-10): same-document View Transitions are Baseline (Oct 2025, Firefox 144); CSS anchor positioning is Baseline (Jan 2026, Firefox 147); Popover API and @starting-style are Baseline 2024; scroll-driven animations are not Baseline (Firefox still behind a flag); appearance:base-select and interpolate-size are Chromium-only. Corporate locked-down browsers lag, so always feature-detect and fall back.
For finance-heavy filters, period presets (MTD/QTD/YTD/1Y/3Y/5Y) plus native <input type=month/date> beat calendar widgets. Calendars (Air Datepicker) are optional.

Icon pairing: Lucide (ISC, 24px/2px stroke) as the primary set plus Tabler Icons (MIT, same grid, 366 finance/chart glyphs), with lu-/tb- id prefixes. Avoid icon webfonts (Tabler 507 KB, Phosphor ~150 KB per weight) and Phosphor's CDN-injecting index.js.
